:bar_chart: _Monthly stability review — 2026-05_
Full report: <https://github.com/bgrady-method/triage-bot/blob/main/stability-reviews/2026-05/report.md>


Executive Summary
• Triage-bot processed *~97 new alerts* across the window (all in May 1–4 — first month of operation). Breakdown: 0 known-issue-recurrence, 0 false-alarm (KB empty), 0 new-with-clear-fix; majority classified *needs-human* (confidence 0.30–0.67). 6 alerts deduplicated.
• A P0 event on 2026-05-02 (revert of `b1f9358`) drove most alert volume. The Signup Availability SLO entered Alert on 2026-04-29 and remained in Alert at report time. Elasticsearch was blocked (403) for every investigation in the window.
*Top 5 recommendations (ranked by ICE score):*

1. *Add triage bot's execution-environment IP to ES allowlist* — ICE 36.0. Blocks every log-based investigation. Single Elastic Cloud console config change.
2. *Identify prod-new-04 daily scheduled job and add KB false-alarm entry* — ICE 16.0. Eliminates daily DM noise; ~1–2 hours to resolve.
3. *Investigate Signup APM silence and formally define Signup SLO* — ICE 13.5. Signup SLO in Alert 6+ days; APM monitors in No Data for 3+ days. Affects new user acquisition.
4. *Add deploy-time post-flight monitor validation for runtime-core* — ICE 10.8. May 2 revert left 8 DD sub-service monitors dark for 3+ days with no automated re-alert. 3,056% error-budget burn vs proposed 99.95% SLO.
5. *Add client-side retry / graceful degradation for GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync* — ICE 6.3. Fired 3× on May 2; self-resolves but generates unnecessary alert noise.
*Availability snapshot (critical services):*


> Note: this is the first stability-review run. All data is from May 1–4 (4 days vs 30-day window). Trend analysis unavailable. Figures are directionally correct; re-confirm once a full 30-day cycle is logged.

:rotating_light: _new alert — needs human_
Channel: `#alert-runtime-monitoring`  -  confidence: 0.72  -  bug-type guess: code/config  -  alerts in group: 2

*Symptoms:*
• `RTC Screen Load` p95 latency has been elevated above the 3s threshold since at least 09:45 EDT (13:45 UTC) — *sustained, not a transient spike*
• Worst spike: *10.08s p95 at 09:54 EDT* and *7.16s at 10:45 EDT* on `POST /api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid*` (threshold: 3s)
• `runtime-core-api` global p90 also spiked: 1.52s at 10:32 EDT, 1.67s at 10:35 EDT, *2.74s at 10:46 EDT* (normal baseline ~0.35s)
• `runtime-core-api` request rate stepped up from ~55 req/s → ~75 req/s after 10:40 EDT (possible retry amplification)
• XHR `status:0` errors on `GET /gateway/syncutil/syncwidget/*/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync` affecting ≥5 accounts: `goodchemistry`, `deltakits1`, `boninfantefriction2`, `wplastics`, `BonOpusSales` — *ongoing as of 11:11 EDT*
• Synthetics monitors 121308660 + 133625690 ("Method UI Grid and Dropdown Performance") in *Alert* state since 09:48–09:53 EDT
*Note:* This is GROUP A (10:04 EDT). 6 additional alert groups from the same root cause are being DM'd separately (B–G, covering 10:15–11:01 EDT).

*Trace IDs:* None recoverable (no server-side error logs in DD; ES returned 403)

*Likely cause:*
Yesterday 2026-05-04 at 15:56 EDT, `runtime-core` merged a revert of _"raise builder MaxUserBundlePairs 2→30"_ (PR #2660). This rolled the `MaxUserBundlePairs` setting back to 2. This controls thread-pool concurrency for the screen builder. If yesterday's runtime monitors fired at ~18:52 UTC (2:52 PM EDT) and recovered, today's load may have re-saturated the reduced pool. The `IIS pool recycle` or `config change to MaxUserBundlePairs` on prod would confirm/deny this.

*Suggested next action:* Check current prod `MaxUserBundlePairs` value (app config / IIS env) and compare to staging. If 2, increase to 30 (or merge a revert-of-revert). Also investigate whether `/gateway/syncutil/syncwidget` service is healthy independently.

:rotating_light: _new alert — needs human_ :warning: ONGOING OUTAGE
Channel: alert-frontend-errors  -  confidence: 0.70  -  bug-type guess: env  -  alerts in group: 2

*Symptoms:*
• 2 frontend error alerts at 11:27am and 11:32am EDT
• *Syncwidget XHR failures (status=0) are affecting 34+ accounts and have been ongoing since at least 7:20am EDT* — this is a pre-existing 5-hour outage, not a new issue
• Endpoint failing: `GET /gateway/syncutil/syncwidget/{account}/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync` — status_code 0 (connection refused/reset at TCP level)
• Accounts confirmed affected: dellamar, wplastics, socalfencesupply32, gtsimulators, mobilitycityofspringfield, holdit, mnjenterprisellc, sumakenorthamericaMT, aosolutions + 25 more
• This path routes through `ms-gateway-api` → likely `ms-sync-util` or `legacy-syncservice-api`; status 0 suggests backend is *completely unreachable* (not returning any HTTP response)
• RTC Screen Load p95 also elevated this morning (2.6s at 11:30am EDT, 3.05s at 11:36am EDT vs 3s threshold); may be separate
• Monitor 77419271 ("Unusual number of XHR errors for account") fired at 11:59am EDT when XHR error count exceeded 40/5min threshold for at least one account
*Trace IDs:* none retrieved (ES unavailable — 403; DD backend logs returned empty)

*Likely cause:* `ms-sync-util` or the `syncutil` IIS pool is down or unreachable. Status 0 (TCP-level failure) across all accounts consistently points to the backend service being completely offline, not returning errors. The syncwidget route in `ms-gateway-api` is routing to a dead backend.

*Suggested next action:* *Urgent* — recycle `ms-sync-util` app pool or check if the service process is alive. Check IIS pool for `ms-sync-util`/`syncutil` virtual app on `microservices.methodlocal.int`. Check `legacy-syncservice-api` (IIS `legacy` pool) if syncwidget is in that service. This has been failing for 5+ hours affecting 34+ customer accounts.
